subject: [PATCH v7 0/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Make the queue depths tunable, and shrink them in a kdump kernel

2026-09-25.patch_summary: This patch series makes the queue depths in the ARM SMMUv3 IOMMU tunable, allowing them to be adjusted based on system requirements. The queues are currently sized from the IDR1 maximum and allocated at probe, which can consume megabytes of memory per queue per SMMU instance. In a kdump kernel, this can lead to out-of-memory errors due to limited crashkernel reservations. The patch series introduces a module parameter cmdq_max_n_shift that allows the command queue depth to be adjusted, and applies it in non-kdump kernels. This reduces the memory consumption of the queues from megabytes to kilobytes, allowing kdump kernels to save vmcores successfully.

reviews.author: Will Deacon
reviews.summary: Reviewer Will Deacon acknowledged the patch and stated he doesn't have a strong opinion on the naming, indicating his approval of the logic.
reviews.raw_body:
Ah, sorry, I missed that you'd already sent a v7! As I said on v6, I don't
have a particularly strong opinion on the naming, so given that Jason is
happy with the logic, I'll just apply this now as-is.

Cheers,

Will

reviews.author: Will Deacon
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where cmdq_max_n_shift is set to a value greater than IDR1_MAX, which could lead to an out-of-bounds allocation.
reviews.raw_body:
Applied to iommu (arm/smmu/updates), thanks!
